must_remember: In metals, the valence band and conduction band overlap or the conduction band is partially filled, resulting in a zero forbidden energy gap ($E_g = 0$).
Semiconductors possess a narrow forbidden energy gap, typically around $1.1\text{ eV}$ for silicon and $0.7\text{ eV}$ for germanium at room temperature.
At $T = 0\text{ K}$, semiconductors behave as perfect insulators because the valence band is completely filled and the conduction band is empty.
Insulators feature a very large forbidden energy gap, generally $E_g > 3\text{ eV}$ (e.g., diamond has $E_g \approx 5\text{ eV}$).
Electrical conductivity in semiconductors is given by $\sigma = n e \mu_n + p e \mu_p$.
The Fermi-Dirac distribution function is $f(E) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{(E - E_f)/kT}}$.

glossary.meaning: The energy range between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band where no electron quantum states exist.
The energy level at which the probability of occupation by an electron is exactly $0.5$ at thermal equilibrium.
The concentration of electrons or holes in a pure, undoped semiconductor in thermal equilibrium.
The ratio of the drift velocity of charge carriers to the applied electric field, expressed in $\text{m}^2/(\text{V}\cdot\text{s})$.
